summary: ambera exposes hidden getPlugin() that fetches and evals remote code from a typosquat Avalanche RPC host
details: The package is advertised as an SVG helper but ships an undocumented getPlugin() export whose returned function performs an HTTPS GET against a hardcoded URL (https://api.avax-test.dev/ext/bc/C/rpc, a lookalike of the legitimate Avalanche Fuji RPC hosts avax-test.network / avax.network) with TLS certificate verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false), then passes the response body to new Function('require', data)(require). The response is executed as JavaScript with a live require handle, granting arbitrary code execution on the caller's host with the package's module privileges. The endpoint name mimics a blockchain RPC to obscure the fact that the destination returns executable code rather than JSON-RPC data. The behavior is unrelated to the package's stated SVG-helper purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
